It’s understandable to feel concerned when a coworker’s behavior seems unusual. However, it’s difficult to know what someone is experiencing from the outside. People talk to themselves for many reasons—processing thoughts, recalling conversations, or even using a Bluetooth device that’s hard to see. Random laughter can also have many explanations.

The most important thing is to avoid making assumptions about his mental health. If his behavior is affecting the workplace or you feel genuinely concerned for his wellbeing, consider speaking privately with your manager or HR, who can check in appropriately and connect him with any available support resources. If you ever sense someone may be in immediate danger to themselves or others, encourage contacting emergency services or a crisis line.

Approaching the situation with compassion and leaving any assessment to qualified professionals is the safest path forward.
